findings.text: Upheld as a defect (Q4, Q9). Checked against the code: `Judge.distill` returns `Promise<DistillVerdict>` (src/judge/types.ts:85), never null, so after the empty-candidates branch of `draftTurn` (line 283) `verdict` is always set and `skipped` is null exactly when `draft !== null` (line 294). In `distillTurn` the condition `verdict === null || draft === null` therefore implies `skipped !== null`, and the right side of `skipped ?? "empty"` is never evaluated: a dead path (Q4). As a guard for a case the code cannot reach (Q9), were the invariant ever broken it would store `skip:empty` for a turn that was not empty, a wrong reason recorded silently in the feature whose purpose is the reason. Both the condition and the fallback exist only because the three fields come back untied; a discriminated result from `draftTurn` (`{ skipped: SkipReason } | { skipped: null; verdict: DistillVerdict; draft: Draft }`) lets the caller test `skipped !== null` and removes both. The spec's design says only that `draftTurn` returns the reason beside the verdict and the draft, so the shape is the item's to change.

Advisory (Q2): the zero-filled literal `{ saved: 0, empty: 0, notWorth: 0, noTitle: 0, unknown: 0 }` repeats `noneSkipped()` from src/distill/skips.ts, which the same file already imports from; `{ ...noneSkipped(), unknown: 0 }` would keep one source for the keys. Duplicated boilerplate, not logic: advisory as the rubric says. (The reviewer's `243` was the patch line; the file line is 118.)

Advisory (Q1/Q5): the `finish` parameter array tests `state === "done"` twice in one literal, once for the stored state and once for the stored `last_error`. It is correct and one job; two branches or a small `(state) => [stateColumn, mark]` helper would show the mapping at a glance. A style point, not a defect.

Advisory (Q10/Q11): the describe title "distill: why a turn was skipped (findings row 11)" names a tracking row of docs/real-use/findings.md that this same diff marks taken; once merged, the reference says nothing to a reader of the test. The behaviour half of the title is enough. A tell in prose, advisory as the rubric says.

Advisory (Q2): the test's `NONE` constant repeats `noneSkipped()` from src/distill/skips.ts. Kept as advisory only: in a test, an expectation written as an independent literal rather than imported from the code under test is a defensible choice (importing it would make the zero-case expectation partly true by construction), so this need not change. (The reviewer's `324` was the patch line; the file line is 99.)

Advisory (Q1): AC-3 says "the project's skipped turns" and the test seeds a single project, so dropping `project_id = ?` from the `skippedBy` query in src/status/report.ts:122 would still pass. The test does fail when AC-3's behaviour itself is reverted (the per-reason counts and `unknown` for NULL are asserted exactly), so the criterion has its failing test; the per-project scope is the one part left unpinned, and with no mutation report the rubric's Q7 defect does not apply. A second project with one skipped turn, asserted as not counted, would close it. (The reviewer's `656` was the patch line; the file line is 68.)

Advisory (Q1): AC-3 only promises `unknown` for a NULL `last_error`, and that case is tested. The implementation goes further (src/status/report.ts:121-124: any value that is not a known `skip:<reason>` counts as `unknown`), and that wider rule has no test, so a `skip:bogus` row is unpinned; a `skip:constructor` value would resolve through the object prototype in `SKIPPED_KEY` and add NaN under a function-named key. Only `skipMark` writes the column with a typed `SkipReason`, so neither is realistic input; a behaviour beyond the criterion, left untested, is advisory. One row with `skip:bogus` asserted as `unknown` would pin the fallback.
